name: Move empty orders to the back
returns: the same list, changed in place
brief:
`qty` holds the quantities of a queue of orders. Fully cancelled orders show a quantity of 0. Move every 0 to the end of the list, keeping the other orders in their order. Change the list in place and return it.

Write `push_empty_to_back(qty)`.

Example. `[0, 5, 0, 3, 12]` becomes `[5, 3, 12, 0, 0]`.
constraints: $0 \le n \le 200{,}000$ quantities, each a whole number; a negative one is a sell and stays.
$O(n)$ time is the target. Calling `remove(0)` or `pop(i)` once per zero is too slow.
All tests share a 5-second time limit. The test checks that the returned list is `qty` itself.
hint: Keep a write position. Copy each non-zero quantity to it and step it on; once the pass ends, fill the rest with zeros.

examples.note: The non-zero orders keep their order: 5, then 3, then 12.
Negative quantities are sells, not empty orders, so they stay at the front.

tests.call: (lambda a: push_empty_to_back(a) is a and a)([0, 4])

how: Submit runs 11 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: One write position compacts the non-zero orders to the front in a single pass.
Building a new list and returning it fails the check that the same list comes back.
One pass plus the fill, so $O(n)$ time and $O(1)$ extra space.
